::: {.why}
The first signal in the book whose input is not a price, which means its failure modes are data-quality failures rather than statistical ones, and those are the ones your pipeline has not been tested against.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Build an accruals signal from EDGAR data and report the fraction of the universe it covers on each date.
- Say what happens to a cross-sectional signal when coverage is not random with respect to the thing you are predicting.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build the signal both ways, from balance sheet changes and from the cash flow statement, and compare them. Where they disagree the cause is usually acquisitions or a tag you mapped wrongly, and finding out which is the real work of a fundamental pipeline.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Audit the coverage, which is the part that matters more than the signal: report the fraction of the universe with a usable value on each date, and compare the forward returns of the covered and uncovered groups. If they differ, your signal has a selection effect that no amount of neutralisation will remove.
:::
:::

## Resources

- [SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (quarterly XBRL)](https://www.sec.gov/data-research/sec-markets-data/financial-statement-data-sets) [data]{.res-kind}
- [Novy-Marx (2012) — The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium](https://mysimon.rochester.edu/novy-marx/research/OSoV.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
An accruals signal with both constructions compared, plus a coverage audit reporting whether missingness is related to forward returns.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your fundamental signal covers 70 percent of the universe. What would you check before believing its information coefficient?
:::
